To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
well-aligned NDFs with a length-to-thickness ratio over 1000 can be prepared on a large scale by drying a uniform-sized (∼4 nm), acid-treated ND dispersion from an aqueous suspension.

well-aligned rectangular-shaped nanofiber films with a length-to-thickness ratio of over 10,000 were formed via a self- assembly process by drying nanodiamonds (ND) of a uniform size (4 nm) from a dilute aqueous solution.

large-scale NDFs and/or NDTFs have been fabricated via a simple self-assembly process of acid-treated nanodiamonnds in water, and their formation was found to be controlled by the delicate interplay among the ND–ND (van der Waals), ND–H2ODipole, and ND–surface interactions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the large-scale self-assembly and bandgap engineering of nanodiamonds via the drying process.
the formation of well-aligned nanodiamond fibers and nanodiamond films via a self-organizing process.

a new approach for the fabrication of large-scale NDFs and their thin films with a well-defined structure and property, and the results obtained are expected to be of great importance for the fabrication of novel functional materials and the understanding of the self-assembly of nanodiamonds in solution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the self-assembly of NDs into NDFs and/or NDTFs is a universal and versatile approach, and can be realized in a variety of solvents and under different drying conditions.
the formation of the NDFs and the NDTFs results from the delicate interplays of ND–ND, H2O–ND, and ND–surface interactions, under the water evaporation-induced directional convections.

the formation of nanodiamond thin films or fibers is a result of the delicate interplay among the ND–ND interaction, the ND–H2 O interaction, and the ND–substrate interaction under the water-evaporating-induced directional convection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the self-assembly process is an efficient and scalable approach to fabricate nanodiamond fibers, films, and related nanocomposites, and the resultant nanodiamons assemblies are of great potential for applications such as transparent conductors, transparent electrodes, and field-emission devices.

the self-assembly of nanodiamonds can be controlled to form either NDFs or NDTFs by simply adjusting the pH and temperature of the aqueous ND dispersions, which provides a new route to fabricate large-scale nanodiamond-based materials for various applications.

NDFs and NDNTFs can be formed on a large scale via a self- assembly process by drying acid treated nanodiamonds from an aqueous dispersion, which would provide a promising approach to the fabrication of large scale nanodiamond based devices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a simple drying process of a nanodiamond suspension can lead to the formation of a large-scale nanodiamond assembly with a high degree of anisotropic alignment.

the formation of nanodiamond assemblies via the self-assembly process can be achieved on a large-scale by controlling the drying condition, and that the resultant assemblies are promising for applications in the optoelectronic and photovoltaic fields, as well as the energy-storage field.
the self-assembly of nanodiamonds into well-aligned nanodiamond fibers and thin films can be realized on a large scale via simple drying of nanodiamond dispersion from an aqueous suspension.
